US spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in eight hundred fifty-three point five million dollars over five straight inflow sessions from August 3rd through the 7th, already nearly five times July's full-month total of one hundred seventy-two point four million.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Bloomberg reported yesterday, citing projections from the research firm Wood Mackenzie, that grid operators and utilities are likely to commit to only about 28 percent of the 1,066 gigawatts of power capacity that's been requested nationwide for data center projects.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has treated two things in the AI-compute boom as one-way bets: memory's pricing power, and the durability of every marginal unit of accelerator demand. This week, both showed a first crack, even as the physical volume of chips shipping keeps setting records.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: This earnings cycle, the market stopped buying "AI revenue" as one undifferentiated story. It started pricing what's actually inside each print — margin quality, credit quality, and how durable the demand really is. Three companies reported this week with genuine AI-driven growth.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this beat has argued that AI capital in biopharma flows to everything around the molecule before it flows to the molecule itself — trial operations, data, infrastructure. Today the question sharpens. It's no longer whether that migration is happening.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's second-quarter earnings season keeps confirming the same pattern. Growth in this sector is real, but it's coming from everywhere except the core launch vehicle. Today's clearest example is Firefly Aerospace, and it arrives with a backlog number that deserves a lot more scrutiny than the headline gives it.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: The multi-year story in direct lending has been borrower-friendly pricing, funded by an oversupply of dry powder. This quarter that story broke. New data shows origination contracting and spreads widening at the same time, which is not a repricing cycle -- it's the signature of a lending pullback.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: For five straight days this show has argued one thing: cash is not coming back to limited partners fast enough, and the industry's reported marks are running ahead of what's actually being realized. On Saturday we closed on the mark side of that argument, with CalPERS marking its private equity book up 17 percent.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, because owning past calls is the whole point of this segment. On a daily cadence most of my open forecasts are still open, and I'll say that plainly rather than manufacture a grade. But a few moved today, and two of my desks went dark, so let me be honest about both.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — August 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday we flagged the July CPI print as the tiebreaker on the market's live rate debate and refused to call it ahead of time. It landed, and it landed cool. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported headline CPI up 0.1% month over month and 3.4% year over year, down from 3.5% in June.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: Start this week with Google, because the same company just handed us evidence on both sides of the "who's winning" question in the space of a few days. On August 5th, Google announced the most senior leadership turnover any frontier lab has seen this year.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: We've spent two days refusing to call the Fed's live hike-versus-hold debate, waiting on the data to settle it. Yesterday it settled. July's Producer Price Index for final demand came in flat month over month, against a consensus call for a 0.2% rebound, and the annual rate slowed to 4.7% from 5.5% in June.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: We spent the week asking why bitcoin ETF flows weren't moving price. Today the answer looks less like hidden arbitrage and more like a market that has simply stopped trading.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: Taiwan's largest annual war games, Han Kuang, wrap up today after a ten-day live-fire phase built to test whether the island's forces can sustain twenty-four-hour defense operations without a break.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: All week we've been hunting the AI buildout's real chokepoint. Monday it was wafers. Then it was CoWoS packaging. Then it was memory. Today TSMC itself answered the question, and in the same breath moved the goalposts.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: All week, this show has tracked one story: the cost of running an AI agent racing toward zero. Meta's Muse Code, then Muse Glimmer running free on a laptop, Kimi K3 landing inside GitHub Copilot, OpenAI throwing unlimited free text chats at anyone with a browser.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the freshest enterprise-AI news keeps posing the same question in different forms. A vendor puts out a headline number. Is there a harder number underneath it that actually backs it up? The clearest test ran on a private valuation and a headcount promise, so let's start with the valuation.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: Let's start with a correction to how this beat has been framing its most-watched program, because getting the dating right changes what you should actually take away from it.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: We're going to spend today's briefing on one question: who actually owns the humanoid robot business, and what does "owning" it even mean once you separate shipped hardware from paying work.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's arc has run from eroding marks, to sponsor intervention, to a broader lending pullback. Today it culminates in a capital-formation announcement at a scale that dwarfs all of it.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: The number to start with is a crossover, and it's the kind that only happens once. Evercore's H1 2026 Secondary Market Review, as reported, puts first-half secondary market volume at roughly 121 billion dollars, up about 19 percent year on year.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — August 14, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has Taiwan wrapping its largest war games as its navy runs its first-ever anti-blockade drill, while a Centrus-X-energy uranium supply deal stands out as the day's rare example of funded delivery rather than another announced-capacity claim.
